studies.label: Formal user study: Low, Medium, and Intensive control of research-ideation agents

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 5.3.1, exclusions and analyzed sample
counts_source.quote: This resulted in 51 valid data points, with 17 for each control level.

arms.name: Low
arms.description: Researchers provide keywords and generate, select, and customize seed ideas; subsequent literature selection, proposal writing, critique, and revision are automated, without steering the Writer or Evaluator (PDF p. 8, Table 3 and Section 3.3.1).

arms.name: Medium
arms.description: Researchers select literature, prompt section-level revisions, customize evaluation criteria, and select agent-suggested improvements; direct text editing, inline revision, and feedback on agent critiques are unavailable (PDF p. 8, Table 3 and Section 3.3.1).

arms.name: Intensive
arms.description: Researchers have the Medium controls plus direct content editing, inline text prompting, feedback on agent critiques, and customization of suggested improvements (PDF p. 8, Table 3 and Section 3.3.1).

studies.country: United States, Jamaica, France, Korea, Canada, Germany, and India in the recruited sample (PDF p. 31, Appendix E, Table 8); locations of retained participants are not separately reported.
studies.task: Researchers generate ideas in their own research area and develop proposals containing literature synthesis, research goals, and a study plan, saving satisfactory drafts and choosing their best draft (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 5.1; PDF p. 29, Appendix C.2).

ai_tool.name: ResearchGuru: GPT-4.1 for Ideator and Writer; Claude Sonnet 3.7 for Evaluator
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 3.3.2 (final system models and Figure 2 caption for ResearchGuru); model release years are not stated.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Participant-level count of unique research proposals from interaction logs. Table 4 reports means and SDs per hour; this normalization is retained. estimates.notes: This contrast retains the two full-arm summaries; no pairwise difference, SE, confidence interval, test, p-value, or standardized effect is printed. Table 4 gives a three-arm omnibus ANOVA, which is not assigned to this pairwise record. Appendix F.1 and Tables 9-10 concern other logged actions, not unique-proposal fluency (PDF pp. 30 and 32). The participant-level SDs and per-arm counts establish the level of the available summaries; se_basis=participant does not imply that a pairwise SE was printed. The paper prints the overall study count and per-arm counts, but no total specifically for this pair; n_total is left null rather than summed. For ai_design, treatment is the arm with greater human control. The same participants recur in the other configuration comparisons, so these estimates are dependent.

open_items: The operational rule distinguishing a unique research proposal from a revision is not stated. The printed hourly normalization is retained without conversion to a raw count (PDF pp. 12-14, Sections 5.3.1 and 6.1, Table 4).

Generate_seed_ideas is not defined clearly enough to separate function invocations from individual returned ideas; excluded pending clarification of the logged event (PDF p. 14, Table 4; PDF p. 30, Appendix D).

Actual total and arm-specific counts at random assignment are not separately established; Section 5.2 describes recruitment and target allocation, while Section 5.3.1 gives analyzed counts. All n_randomized fields remain null (PDF pp. 12-13).

No pairwise total sample count, pairwise test, difference, SE, interval, or standardized effect is printed for unique-proposal fluency. Only arm means, SDs, counts, and an omnibus test are available (PDF pp. 13-14; PDF pp. 30 and 32, Appendix F.1 and Tables 9-10).

Task duration differs between the main procedure and the scripted instructions: 35-40 minutes in Section 5.1 versus 30 minutes in Appendix C.2. The implemented duration for every participant is not established (PDF pp. 11-12 and 29).
The release years of the named final-study models are not printed. ai_tool.year is null; data-collection dates are not substituted for model release dates (PDF pp. 10-12).

Overlap between development or usability pilots and the formal sample is not documented, and no reuse of another paper’s sample is stated. shared_sample remains null; pilot participants are not added to the formal analyzed sample (PDF p. 11, Sections 4.1-4.2; PDF p. 12, Section 5.2; PDF p. 27, Appendix B).
notes:
Extracted on 2026-10-11. Read the complete markdown conversion from beginning to end, including references and all appendices, then extracted the cited PDF pages with pymupdf. PDF page indices plus one agree with printed page numbers. Table 4 text preserves the arm-column order and printed means/SDs. Sources retain printed precision, including 1.20. No effects, differences, standard errors, or pairwise sample totals were computed.

S1 alone supplies eligible estimates. It is an individually randomized between-person experiment: "participants were randomly assigned to Low, Medium, or Intensive control levels" (PDF p. 11, Section 5.1). It is coded lab_rct because sessions were supervised through Zoom screen sharing, with academic-network recruitment rather than an online panel (PDF p. 12, Section 5.2). The mixed population comprises PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, professors, and research scientists. The AI role is other because ResearchGuru integrates idea generation, literature synthesis, proposal drafting, critique, and revision in a structured notebook workflow; the interface excludes chat (PDF p. 8, Section 3.3.1; PDF p. 10, Section 3.3.2).

The analyzed sample follows exclusions based on the post-task survey distribution: "Three data points were identified as extreme ratings: two unusually low and one unusually high." (PDF p. 13, Section 5.3.1; PDF text line-break hyphenation normalized.) This post-treatment exclusion rule is retained as an analysis limitation. Recruitment and target allocation are not treated as confirmed randomization-stage counts.

There is no no-AI arm, across-person output-diversity measure, or unassisted post-AI creative task. Post-task survey timing does not establish an after_ai output. Self-reports, workflow-action counts, model-output evaluations, and qualitative or illustrative cases are enumerated in not_extracted. No subgroup, mediation, or model-only result is used as an eligible estimate. The three retained contrasts reuse the same study arms and are not independent samples.
